data.title: Skeleton
data.tagline: Reserve the layout while content is loading
data.description: A skeleton roughly matches the shape of incoming content so the page stays stable during a short load. It should not be a detailed gray copy of every element. For a tiny action or an unknown layout, a simpler loading indicator may be clearer.

use: Profile content with a known shape
A page where layout stability matters
Short waits before real content appears
avoid: Show a skeleton for a task with no known layout
Keep it running after a request failed
Animate a complex placeholder that distracts from the page
Use it to hide a consistently slow experience

lessonPractice.title: An article list has a known layout, but its data usually takes one or two seconds to arrive. How can loading reduce layout movement?

options.label: Reserve image and title shapes with a skeleton, then replace it with data
options.feedback: A skeleton that resembles the incoming structure reserves space and reduces movement when real content appears.

options.label: Show 'No articles yet' first and replace it when data arrives
options.feedback: The request is still pending, so an empty state incorrectly claims that no data exists.

options.label: Animate a progress bar from 0% without reading actual progress
options.feedback: The system does not know completion percentage, and fake progress does not reserve the article layout.

data.agentPrompt: While article data is pending, show a skeleton matching the real image and title layout, then replace it in place. On failure, switch to an error and retry instead of keeping the skeleton. Confirm that content arrival causes no obvious layout jump.
